futureImplementationCandidates.candidate: Reserve distinct routing lanes for different tensors that currently have positive-length collinear spans; retain shared-tensor spans where binding and roles justify sharing.
futureImplementationCandidates.requiredFutureEvidence: Compare current/new typed endpoint bindings and expansion projection; inspect complete SVG and actual pixel output at85/180mm; verify pinned/moved positions and export consistency before any acceptance claim.

futureImplementationCandidates.candidate: Reduce different-tensor crossings by local reroute after lane separation; preserve fixed node positions and container boundaries.
futureImplementationCandidates.requiredFutureEvidence: Quantify route crossings and detours, retain spatial continuity, and review pixel line/arrow clarity rather than relying on nominal body clearance.

futureImplementationCandidates.candidate: For same-tensor overlaps, first review role-specific style and shared-source semantics. If deliberate sharing is retained, add consistent junction semantics or differentiate branches when needed.
futureImplementationCandidates.requiredFutureEvidence: Do not silently merge distinct role-specific edges; inspect canonical edge IDs, projected boundary ports, and visible style before deciding.

limits: Candidates ranked for review only, not authorized/applied code changes, defect proof or publication acceptance. Different tensor crossing/overlap is not automatically unnecessary or wrong; same tensor geometry is not automatically intentional/correct.
Counts are exact serialized segment incidences, not unique pixel intersection/net counts. Point touches may duplicate a bend incidence.
No image view or target-scale legibility certification in this structure-only report. A good endpoint match and zero main card penetration do not resolve route distinguishability.
Do not infer browser capture timing, screenshot cause, model runtime correctness, performance, or human approval.
Input source geometry reports retain every existing route warning and exact per-case raw binding.
